clearedSpotChecks.check: L-732. Which reth revision do the public MegaETH locks name, and does its execution cache keep stale storage for an account that was destroyed and re-created without code in one block?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.3.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs. At lines 903-923 a destroyed account whose original info had no code is removed from account_cache and the loop continues, so its new storage is not written. A destroyed account that had code clears the whole cache (self.clear()). The PoolManager, and every token and hook an existing pool uses, has code at the start of any block, so the bad branch cannot keep stale storage for them. Only an address that was empty at block start is affected, and a contract placed there is the attacker's own, which is at most pool-creator level. I did not confirm the mega-reth revision; that repository is private, as the item says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-738. Do mined v3 style swaps on HyperEVM, produced by the closed hl-node validator, match the exact FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and TickMath formulas of src/libraries?
clearedSpotChecks.note: tools/opdiff/v4math.py:53-80 matches src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-120 line for line: the mulmod with not(0), the prod1 borrow, the remainder subtraction, the twos factor, six Newton steps, and the round-up check. The raw files agree with the stated counts. Stage B ran 2,995 + 3,000 + 5,000 + 20,000 = 30,995 groups with 0 + 0 + 1 + 3 = 4 mismatches. The planted MULMOD and tick faults produced 131 and 117 mismatches. The liquidity sum given for 0x47a2f2ff is correct. The coverage is a sample, and the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and amounts at or above 2^160 have no mined instance. The item says both of these plainly, so the clearance holds only for the branches that were exercised.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-728. Has any mined PoolManager transaction on MegaETH or HyperEVM called clear(), with an exact credit or otherwise?
clearedSpotChecks.note: keccak256("clear(address,uint256)") computed with tools/opdiff/evm.py starts 0x80f0b44c, which is the selector the scan uses (clearscan.py:20). It matches src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:194. The scan walks every nested frame into the PoolManager. Line counts are 51,071 + 162 = 51,233 on MegaETH and 2,782 + 1 = 2,783 on HyperEVM, and no line contains 80f0b44c. The set leaves out transactions with no log and no token transfer, which the item says. clear at src/PoolManager.sol:310-319 only removes a credit the caller already holds, so even a mistake here would not take funds from others. A side check of L-748: eth_getCode of 0xc20699185c15D0a2fD65779BB5d69f5b0B113c00 on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com returns 0x, and the nonce goes from 0 at block 0x23db26a to 1 at block 0x23db26b (37,597,803). The block number is right, but the hex label 0x23db20b in that item's source is wrong: it is block 37,597,707.
